The words

Our Father in heaven, we hallow thy name!
May thy kingdom holy on earth be the same!
O give to us daily our portion of bread;
It is from thy bounty that all must be fed.

Forgive our transgressions, and teach us to know
That humble compassion which pardons each foe:
Keep us from temptation, from weakness and sin,
And thine be the glory forever — Amen.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Ab and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s, (E♭), on the word “Our”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 2/2 means two minim beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m s l — only 5 different notes, so it is a good one for a choir new to solfa. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Sarah Josepha Hale wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 437 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Lord's Prayer”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens (11.11.11.11), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FOUNDATION (FUNK); any other Elevens tune fits them as well.

  • Words: Sarah Josepha Hale (1788–1879)
  • Music (1832): Joseph Funk (1778–1862)

Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune FOUNDATION (FUNK) by Joseph Funk (1778–1862); words by Sarah Josepha Hale (1788–1879). Questions about Our Father in Heaven, We Hallow Thy Name

What is the doh of Our Father in Heaven, We Hallow Thy Name?

In this version, in Ab major, doh is Ab. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Our Father in Heaven, We Hallow Thy Name start on?

It starts on s, (E♭ in Ab major), a pickup on the word “Our” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s,.

Is Our Father in Heaven, We Hallow Thy Name in the public domain?

Yes. Sarah Josepha Hale died in 1879, Joseph Funk died in 1862; the words were in print by 1853 and the music in 1832. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
